Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 36dba30ad1af598bc4b30d0b38f4911a3c8b93f5
We don't need these prefix in the header. It is just eating up the space. Instead some meaningful information can be added?
Done
Don;t need this. Defining in constants make sense when it means something else w.r.t the context else it will just add an overhead.
Done
If possible, please break the commit in chunks below 100 LOC, it is more convenient to review.

> starting bit

This should be only bit position.
Done

> number of bits in keyword

number of bits to be update in the keyword
Done
If I remember, we already had a comment for this?
Yes, addressed it.
nit: attribute?
Done
Better name? like itr to what?
Done

as record size and keyword size are different.
and record name keyword name can't be same. so we don't need left shift operation (which is needed to generate unique hash, in case record and keyword values are same).
Done

empty line required.
API is returning BiosAttributeCurrentValue(std;:variant) not tuple.
Done
isn't it [in,out] ?
Done
it can be "const unsigned char&"
This API is copy-pasted from vpd-manager utility. Addressed this here.

enabled value/max value, disabled value/min value
?

>enabled value/max value, disabled value/min value

We do not care about max/min value for the BIOS attributes here. Only the enabled/disabled value is needed.
okay, do we need to mention that in the comment ?
Addressed this.
need to use bytes not bit for RG.
range should be updated to max value of byte length (255) ?

>need to use bytes not bit for RG.

That would require creating a separate std::map for `VSYS:RG`, which is an unnecessary overhead.

>range should be updated to max value of byte length (255) ?

What do you mean by range here?
in case keyword is in bytes size, enabled value & disabled value fields won't be used.
need new line after this
Done
l_numBits is enough as we referring without keyword here l_bitPosition
`l_numBitsKeyword` gives more context. Do you see an issue here if we use longer variable name?

its not about longer variable name, how we used variable name to describe.
l_numOfBitsUsed or l_numOfBits gives more readability than l_numBitsKeyword which is not giving much sense while understanding it.
As discussed, keeping this variable name unchanged for now.
l_numBytesKeyword is used in case of int64_t type, can we reduce the scope of this variable
Done
l_bitPosition is required only for string type(D1 attributes), can we keep this local.
Done
instead having new variable here, we would have updated l_numBytesKeyword itself ?
Done
instead of hardcoding, can we take sizeof(int64_t)
Done
if the number bytes to copy is more than 1byte, 0 will be assigned for remaining number of bytes.
Addressed this.
why do we need to copy to another variable. as we get (*l_attrVal) value anywhere.

Using `l_valStr` to keep a copy of the attribute value in lower case.
`*l_attrVal` holds the original value read from BIOS Config Manager.
if we are not using it any more, we can modify it. unless original is used later.
Addressed this.
I dint get why do we need this casting, as utils::toLower() takes std::string&
Done
Nit: update single bit on the 0th byte. ?
I think its implicitly understood that we will update a bit on the 0th byte. I do not see a scenario where we will update a bit on some other byte.
Acknowledged

do we need extra variable l_numBitsShift & l_mask, can't we do in place calculation ?
current operation :(*l_attrVal & (l_byteMask << (l_byte * 8))) >> (l_byte * 8)
can we optimise it ?
Addressed this.
new line required after this statement.
Done
can we say getBiosAttribute(), internal thing no need to present as a part of function name. ?

This API has been copied as is from `dbus_utility.hpp`.

`getBiosAttribute()` name is abstract and doesn't make it apparent how/where the attribute is fetched from.
Done

its generic api name as its copying integral data into bytes. 
so can we keep generic name ?
I think the name is generic enough. Please do suggest if you have any better names in mind.
convertIntegralTypeToBytes ?
Done

we can just say number of bytes to copy.
i_numBytes or i_numBytesToCopy is enough?
Done
should the API name getVpdFromBiosConfigManager ?
This change is unrelated to the purpose of this patch.
As discussed, won't be updating the name of the API for now.
should it be VALUE_1 if not found ?
Done
Should it be VALUE_0 ?
Done

This API was copied as is from vpd-manager common_utility.hpp.

https://grok.openbmc.org/xref/openbmc/openpower-vpd-parser/vpd-manager/include/utility/common_utility.hpp?r=fa5e4d325ef9cea3c841fe89d202c340f92bd8c6#111
Acknowledged
why is this called an integral data ?

This API is a generic API which takes in any integral data type(eg. `int16_t` , `int32_t`, `int64_t`, etc) and converts it into binary vector of bytes.

Currently, we get BIOS attribute FCO as an `int64_t` datatype from BIOS Config Manager, which we need to convert into a vector of bytes.
Acknowledged
Feel you tried to write this generic but seems to be tied to what is above , I need a walkthrough for this you understand it.
Done
